rows.description: I blame one parent and cannot sit in the same room with them. Wise: recognise that anger covers sadness and that adult relationships are more complicated than I see. Harmful: cutting one parent off entirely.
I mourn the family I thought I had and feel it as my loss too. Wise: let myself cry, keep routines, and talk to a friend or counsellor. Harmful: pretending I am fine to protect everyone.
After time I see both parents as flawed humans who do better apart, and I take care of my own life. Wise: stay open to visits and honest with them. Risk: forcing calm before I have grieved.
I secretly wonder if my fights or grades caused the split. Wise: hear from the parents plainly that it was not my fault and keep loving both. Harmful: trying to fix them by behaving perfectly.
My classmates return to normal life while I feel frozen, and it hurts that nobody asks. Wise: tell one or two people what I need; grief is invisible unless named. Harmful: assuming nobody cares.

I keep replaying what I should have said before my friend died. Wise: guilt is love with nowhere to go; write him a letter, share memories, talk to someone. Harmful: punishing myself for what I could not have known.

After my father's death, my mother leans on me as if I were the adult. I feel pride and heaviness. Wise: support her while also grieving myself and involving relatives. Harmful: taking on all the roles alone.
Why did God take him? I am angry and a bit ashamed of it. Wise: anger and faith can coexist; allow the questions, seek people with wisdom and patience. Harmful: forced acceptance that hides the pain.

After you reported an issue, you get sidelined and labeled troublemaker. Retaliation is real and not your fault. Keep records, contact a lawyer or regulator, lean on friends, and remember integrity has a cost but keeps you whole.
You went along once and now feel sick about it. Guilt is useful if it leads to repair: come clean where possible, correct the record, and refuse a second time. Wallowing or hiding deepens the harm.

Fear of losing the job, visa or reference makes compliance feel practical. Wise action: write down facts, consult a lawyer or ethics line, and avoid being the only signature. Immature: going along and telling yourself you had no choice.

Boss says fudge the numbers or delay disclosure, hinting at your job. Recognise it as pressure, not a favour. Note the instruction in writing, refuse politely, and know your escalation channel. It is not your fault they asked.
My friend gives me a drawing and I say "thank you, I love it" and hug it. I feel loved and want to give back. Saying thanks kindly teaches me how gifts make friendships warm.
I give Papa a card I made and he puts it on the fridge. I feel proud. A parent who treasures a child's small gift teaches that giving is valued, and that my own effort matters.
I draw a card for my friend's birthday and give it with a big smile. I feel excited that they will like it. Giving something I made myself teaches that love is in the effort, not the price.
The teacher mocked me in front of the class and I wanted to vanish. That was wrong of her. I tell my parents so they can raise it with the school. Adults should correct, not shame.
I am scared of my strict teacher and my hands shake. Fear of getting it wrong blocks learning. I can ask a question after class and see her softer side. Many strict teachers care.
My favourite teacher was unfair to me once, and I am shocked. Adults can make mistakes. I can politely tell her how I felt. Cutting her off forever or mocking her is not needed.
The teacher seems to like some kids more, and I feel invisible. It may be real or not. I do my best, ask for help, and speak to her or a parent if unfair. Sulking helps nobody.
I see friends' holidays, looks and parties and feel left out. Wise: remember they post highlights; limit scrolling time, and message a friend instead.
A post of mine goes viral and I feel a rush. Wise: enjoy it lightly, and do not tie my worth to numbers that will drop.
A friend keeps flashing new things and grades. I sense they compare to feel better than me. Wise: stay warm, avoid competing, and stay grounded in my own values.
I keep posting for likes and feel low when they are few. Wise: notice the loop, post for reasons that are mine, and mute accounts that make me feel less.
